summary: Confirmed errors.json is absent in nvim and drifted (bare array + undocumented fix_status='resolved') in cslib. Found exactly one real inline writer (skill-planner) and two readers, both assuming object-with-array. Recommended one reconciled schema (context superset, fix_status enum + deprecated 'resolved', recurrence_count dropped as computed-not-stored, fixed_date/fix_task kept), and flagged that errors-append.sh needs both append AND update subcommands since errors.json is mutable, unlike events.jsonl.
decisions_made: Object-with-array ({"errors": [...]}) over bare array — both live readers already assume this form, cslib's bare array is the anomaly to fix
fix_status enum expanded to unfixed|in_progress|fixed|resolved, with resolved documented as a deprecated synonym for fixed (backward-compat only, new writes always use fixed)
recurrence_count dropped from the persisted schema — no writer ever populated it; /errors already describes it as computed at analysis time

errors-append.sh must implement both an append subcommand (mirrors events-append.sh directly) and a novel update subcommand (read-modify-write under flock, no existing precedent) because errors.json records are mutated in place by the documented Fix Mode workflow, unlike append-only events.jsonl
Validation style follows events-append.sh's existing idiom: hand-written bash arg/enum/jq-shape checks kept in sync with the schema doc, not a runtime JSON-Schema-library call

The 'UNBLOCKS: tasks 951/952/953' claim in the task description is thematic, not a real dependency — those tasks explicitly build on events.jsonl instead and carry no dependency edge to/from 979 in state.json
